text:
olivia: Heads-up — I'm kicking off a config-only hotpatch to routing + batching to shave tail latency during the afternoon ramp. Starting canary in eu-west-1 for 10m, then staged rollout. Changes: routing.policy=prefer-low-latency, batch.max=8->6, request.timeout_ms=60000->45000, per_route_qps_limit=200->150. Not touching kv_cache_ttl. @raj @maria please watch dashboards and alerts.

deploy-bot: config-canary STARTED (change_id: cfg-2026-04-13-hotpatch-9). Canary: eu-west-1, 1% traffic. Applying to routing-config:v2026-04-13-hotpatch.

raj: ack. watching p50/p95 and 5xx. Will keep an eye on in-flight requests and queues.

maria: quick question — why reduce batch.max? curious impact on throughput.

olivia: batch.max reduction is to lower tail latency for short seqs — we expect slight increase in token cost but better p95. This is temporary while we validate kernel scheduling changes.

tim: heads-up from SRE: if per_route_qps_limit causes 429 spikes we should soft-ramp the cap (e.g., 200->175->150) with 5 min holds. Can we do staged caps?

olivia: ok, plan: canary uses 150 cap but if we see >0.5% 429 in 5m we'll flip to 175 and alert. If error/latency regressions > threshold we'll rollback.

maria: nit — pin routing config name please so rollbacks are deterministic. Suggest routing-config:v2026-04-13-hotpatch (already in deploy-bot message) and keep previous tag routing-config:v2026-04-11-stable.

olivia: yep pinned. Rollback command: deploy-bot rollback-config cfg-2026-04-13-hotpatch -> routing-config:v2026-04-11-stable.

raj: copying dashboards: https://dash.redwood.internal/latency?range=15m&env=eu-west-1

olivia: embedding the config snippet we applied:
```
{
  "routing": {"policy": "prefer-low-latency", "config_tag": "v2026-04-13-hotpatch"},
  "batching": {"max_batch": 6},
  "timeouts": {"request_ms": 45000},
  "limits": {"per_route_qps": 150}
}
```

deploy-bot: Canary reporting metrics (5m): p50 -14ms, p95 -32ms, errors +0.15% (baseline 0.1%), 429s 0.12%.

sre-bot: Alerting rule note: if 5xx > 0.5% or 429 > 1% for 5m, paging oncall.

tim: looks safe so far. hold for the full 10m and then expand to 10% traffic for 15m.

maria: agree. If 5xx creeps above 0.3% during the 10% stage we revert to v2026-04-11-stable.

olivia: rollout plan updated: 1% -> 10% -> 25% -> 100%, holds between stages: 10m, 15m, 20m. Manual go/no-go at each step.

deploy-bot: Canary completed, promoted to 10% (change_id: cfg-2026-04-13-hotpatch).

raj: spotted a tiny blip in request lat distribution at 10% (p99 +70ms) but p95 still improved. No spike in errors.

maria: note for release notes: "Temporary routing/batching hotpatch to reduce p95; minor QPS limits applied to mitigate node pressure."

olivia: adding to release notes and tagging customer-impact: none.

sre-bot: Monitoring window started for staged rollout to 25%. Next check at +15m.

olivia: rollback threshold repeated here: any sustained 5xx > 0.5% for 5m OR 429 > 1% -> immediate rollback. deploy-bot rollback command tested.

tim: please also add a gradual throttle step if we see 429s rising: script run: `scripts/gradual-qps-ramp cfg-2026-04-13-hotpatch --steps 175,150 --hold 300`

olivia: good call. I'll stand by to run if needed.

deploy-bot: Staged rollout to 25% completed. Metrics stable.

maria: bumping to 50% when ready. watching for any latency regressions on long-seq traffic.

olivia: scheduling 50% now, hold 20m. If stable schedule final 100% in 30m.

raj: all looks green on the dashboards. no abnormal error channels.

deploy-bot: Staged rollout to 50% succeeded. Change is currently at 50% traffic.

olivia: final decision room: if no regressions in 30m we'll push to 100%. If anything crosses thresholds we rollback immediately. Thank you team. :rocket:

maria: thanks — documenting rollback steps in the ticket.

tim: thumbs-up from SRE.

deploy-bot: Change cfg-2026-04-13-hotpatch is at 50%. Next automated step requires manual confirm to go to 100%.
